brand_focus: Cooking tips, recipes, and marinades with AI-styled ingredient photography. Audience is Europe-first, US a strong second. Goal: grow followers fast-but-safe by making every post highly shareable (sent to a friend) and saveable.

slots.note: w1-18 is the highest-volume confirmed slot (7 posts, avg reach 1.7) — most reliable signal in the dataset. Anchor the account's best-reach theme here.
w2-12 reached 2.0 on 1 post — highest single-slot reach observed. Thin sample but promising; brand-core marinade theme earns continued testing to build signal.
w3-12 avg reach 1.7 on 3 posts — confirmed mid-week lunchtime performer. Technique carousels are natural save-bait; continuing this pairing to deepen the sample.

w5-10 reached 2.0 on 1 post; proxying to Thursday morning as an adjacent high-browse window. Quick-dinner earns a second slot as the account's highest-reach theme. Sauce (avg reach 1.5, 6 posts, zero engagement) remains retired.

content_plan.quick-dinner: A complete weeknight dinner built around one hero ingredient that comes together fast. Slide 1: hero shot of the finished dish — rich colour, glossy sauce, clean negative space, pure food photography with absolutely no text, numbers, or labels anywhere on the image. Slide 2: flat-lay of raw ingredients loosely arranged by colour and texture — purely photographic, nothing annotated. Slides 3–4: two-beat visual sequence showing one key technique moment (e.g. a vigorous sear, sauce reducing in pan) followed by the plated result — no text overlays of any kind. Final slide: tight close-up of texture and colour that makes the dish feel craveable and achievable. ALL ingredient quantities, timing, steps, swaps, and any written information belong in the caption only.
content_plan.marinade: One complete marinade built around a single protein or seasonal occasion. Slide 1: hero shot of the marinated, deeply coloured, glistening protein on a clean dark or neutral surface — pure food photography, zero text, numbers, or labels anywhere. Slide 2: aesthetic flat-lay of raw marinade ingredients grouped loosely by colour and texture — purely photographic, nothing annotated. Slides 3–4: visual process contrast — protein submerging into the marinade liquid, then the vivid colour and sheen transformation after marinating — no overlaid text or graphics. Final slide: finished plated dish in warm directional light, garnished but not cluttered. ALL ratios, quantities, timing, substitution tips, and step information belong in the caption exclusively.
content_plan.technique: One foundational cooking technique relevant to home cooks — e.g. how to build a fond, reverse-sear, bloom spices, or emulsify a pan sauce. Slide 1: hero shot of the dramatic visual payoff of the technique (e.g. a perfectly seared crust, a glossy emulsified sauce) — pure food photography, zero text, numbers, labels, or graphics anywhere. Slide 2: flat-lay or close-up of the key tools or ingredients that make the technique work — purely photographic, nothing annotated. Slides 3–4: two-beat before/after visual sequence showing the technique mid-action and the finished result — no text overlays. Final slide: close-up detail of texture, colour, or finish that makes the result unmistakably worth learning the technique. ALL explanations, ratios, timing, troubleshooting tips, and step-by-step instructions belong in the caption exclusively.

caption_strategy: Every caption must earn a save or a send before it earns a like. Open with a single punchy hook sentence that names the dish or technique and the core benefit (speed, flavour payoff, a surprising trick) — make it search-friendly by including the ingredient or method name naturally. Follow with the full, usable recipe or technique breakdown in the body: quantities, ratios, timing, and swaps all belong here, never on the image. Close with a direct, low-friction CTA that prompts a share or save — e.g. 'Save this before your next grocery run' or 'Send this to the person who always asks what to make for dinner.' Use conversational but confident tone; avoid vague filler phrases. Keep total caption length to 150–250 words.
hashtag_strategy: Use exactly 3–5 hashtags per post, placed at the end of the caption. Prioritise mid-size, ingredient- or technique-specific tags (e.g. #ChickenMarinade, #WeeknightDinner, #CookingTips) over massive generic tags where the account will be buried. Include one broad anchor tag (#HomeCooking or #EasyRecipes) and one niche tag tied to the specific dish or method. Rotate tags post to post to test which drive the most non-follower reach; do not repeat the exact same set two posts in a row. Avoid branded or invented hashtags with no search volume.
learnings: All 22 posts show zero sends, saves, and follows — reach is real but nothing is converting. This is a caption and hook problem, not a slot or theme problem. Priority fix: rewrite captions to lead with a concrete benefit hook and close with an explicit save-or-send CTA every single post. Technique and quick-dinner carousels show the best reach (avg 1.7); double down on these. Retire sauce entirely (6 posts, lowest reach, no engagement). w0-19 (avg reach 1.3) and w6-10 (reach 1.0) are the weakest slots — dropped. Hold cadence at 4 posts/week until saves or sends register.
